claims.text: MJP French edition; English reproduction; Sinhala uncollated

Amiens’s French edition cedes Batavian holdings to Britain. The English-reproduced Kandyan convention vests British sovereignty, reserves chiefs’/customary rights and promises Buddhist protection; Sinhala original uncollated. Sri Lanka’s archive records resistance. Neither establishes universal consent, fulfilled protection or equal lived rights.
Did the 1802 Batavian cession itself transfer the distinct Kandyan polity? Different territorial scopes

claims.text: Why is “all Ceylon transferred in 1802” not supported by these witnesses? Amiens covers Batavian holdings, while the distinct Kandyan polity is addressed by the 1815 convention; the two territorial/institutional scopes differ.

French Amiens edition and English-reproduced Kandyan convention remain distinct, with Sinhala original uncollated. Chiefs are not all Kandyan/Buddhist/Tamil/Muslim/Vedda peoples. Reserved rights and promised protection are not fulfilment; attributed Sri Lankan resistance remains earned evidence. British recipient/sovereign remains explicit with1802 transfer and1815 authority in loaded evidence and Reveal; chief/customary rights, promised Buddhist protection, Sinhala noncollation and attributed resistance remain mandatory.
Original nongeographic schematic and own English factual summaries; no source image or official translation. Selected documentary relations do not establish current borders or residents’ consent.
